flags.title: HSBC China exchange rate
flags.detail: The public HSBC rates page fills its table by script; the numbers used come from the data feed on the same HSBC host, quoted as USD per 1 CNY and inverted here. Confirm the orientation and the figures in a browser.

flags.title: Bank of Communications rate and fee
flags.detail: The board's rows are script-rendered and were not captured; no tariff page was found. All BoCom cost fields are blank.

flags.title: ICBC wire fee
flags.detail: ICBC's price list (effective 2026-08-08) publishes its tables as images. The fee is blank; only the rate margin is shown.

flags.title: China Construction Bank wire fee
flags.detail: Head office publishes no figure and refers to 95533. A 2016 Hebei branch page and a 2012 article on ccb.com both state 0.1% (min ¥20, max ¥300) plus ¥80 cable; treated as a lead and not used. The fee is blank.

flags.title: Bank of China tariff date and channel
flags.detail: The fee comes from the personal e-banking table headed 'from 2014-11-01'. Counter pricing and current promotions were not read; a note on the page says discounts and local differences may apply.

flags.title: ABC and CMB tariff pages are undated
flags.detail: Both pages are live on the banks' sites but carry no effective date. A CMB FAQ gives the cable fee as ¥100-150 rather than ¥150.

flags.title: Board rates are indicative and move
flags.detail: Every board says the rate at the moment of the transaction prevails. The six boards were read within about ten minutes of each other on 2026-11-10 (17:39-17:49 Beijing); the estimates will drift with the market.

flags.title: Charges outside the sending bank
flags.detail: Intermediary-bank deductions and the US bank's incoming-wire fee are not published by the sending banks and depend on your US bank. They are not in any estimate.

flags.title: Which papers a branch accepts
flags.detail: The rule names 'source-of-funds material showing the amounts, including tax vouchers'. Lists of accepted documents, and what happens to old balances with no tax record, are branch practice and not published.

flags.title: Two official definitions of 'domestic individual'
flags.detail: The State Council Regulations (Art. 52) count a foreigner who has lived in China continuously for a year as a domestic individual; the PBOC rules (Art. 37) define the term by Chinese identity document. SAFE's FAQ gives the annual quota only to holders of a Foreign Permanent Resident ID.

flags.title: Annual quota text
flags.detail: The USD 50,000 figure was read as an excerpt of a SAFE page marked 'amended'. The consolidated text was not read by this session.

flags.title: Housing-sale proceeds
flags.detail: The remittance conditions were read from a 2025 consultation draft and a 2017 branch guide, not from the text in force. Taxes on the sale other than 20% income tax on the gain were not verified.

flags.title: Inheritance and emigrant transfers
flags.detail: Corrected 11 November 2026. The 2004 instalment schedule (half, half of the rest after one year, the remainder after two) and the head-office step above ¥500,000 were removed from 10 February 2014 by SAFE Hui Fa [2014] No. 2, Section 6, read in full; method M14 is now priced as one wire instead of three. Still open: no official sentence on Chinese tax on inheritances was found, so that tax cell is blank.

flags.title: Wise fee
flags.detail: The guide links to a pricing page; no fee figure was read. Wise also decides your overall limit from your tax records.

flags.title: Western Union
flags.detail: Nothing was verified from an official page.

flags.title: Card network rate and ATM surcharges
flags.detail: The UnionPay conversion rate and US ATM-owner surcharges were not read. The 0.5% issuer fee is China Merchants Bank's, from an excerpt; other issuers differ.

flags.title: Cost of carrying cash
flags.detail: Flights, the permit and note-withdrawal charges at mainland banks were not published or not read. Only the rate margin on buying notes is shown.

flags.title: Rate for renminbi notes abroad
flags.detail: No official source publishes it.

flags.title: Cross-border renminbi remittance by a foreign individual
flags.detail: Rule not verified in this session.

flags.title: 'No Chinese tax on converting'
flags.detail: No official sentence says this. It is a reading of the income tax law, whose nine categories of taxable income do not include exchanging currency; what the bank asks for is proof that tax on the income was paid.

flags.title: US exchange-gain illustration
flags.detail: Uses IRS yearly average rates as a stand-in for the unknown rates on the days the renminbi was acquired. Whether a conversion is a 'personal transaction' (capital gain above USD 200) or an ordinary section 988 item depends on the facts. The treatment of losses was not quoted from an official source.

flags.title: Treaty and credit limits
flags.detail: The US-China income tax treaty was not read by this session; foreign tax credit limits are individual.

flags.title: Editions
flags.detail: 26 USC 988 is quoted from the 2024 edition of the Code; the eCFR calls itself authoritative but unofficial.

flags.title: Reference mid-rate
flags.detail: The yardstick used to turn renminbi costs into dollars is the average of the mid-points of the five mainland boards read. It is arithmetic, not a published rate.

flags.title: One wire per amount
flags.detail: Each amount is priced as a single wire unless the method says otherwise. Online channels may cap a single wire, which multiplies the fees.

flags.title: Fees charged on top
flags.detail: The estimates add the bank's fees to the renminbi debited. Some banks or fee options deduct them from the amount sent instead.

flags.title: HSBC Global Transfer rate
flags.detail: The tariff gives the fee but not the exchange rate used for Global Transfer. The all-in cost is blank.

flags.title: Sources read only as excerpts
flags.detail: Sources marked 'excerpt' on the Sources page were read as excerpts returned by a search index from the official host, not as full pages. Read the full page before relying on them.

flags.title: Deposit-interest exemption is temporary
flags.detail: The 2008 notice 'temporarily exempts' savings interest; read as an excerpt.

flags.title: Tax-filing form above USD 50,000
flags.detail: Announcement 2013 No. 40 lists a foreign individual's pay among items needing a filing above USD 50,000 per payment, and in Article 4 sends foreign individuals back to the personal foreign-exchange rules. How a bank applies this to your own salary is practice.

flags.title: Quota route pricing
flags.detail: Priced at Bank of China's rate and fee with one wire per calendar year; any bank may be used.
